bill.summary:
Renewed Hope Act
This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to hire additional personnel, enhance coordination among agencies, and establish a training program to support child sexual exploitation investigations within Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). HSI is the principle investigative arm of DHS and has broad authority to investigate a wide range of illegal activities, including child sexual exploitation.
Specifically, this bill directs DHS to hire, train, and assign 200 forensic analysts and child exploitation investigators to the Victim Identification Laboratory and to field offices throughout the United States to support the identification of victims of child sexual exploitation. The bill provides direct-hire authority (i.e., an expedited hiring authority) to DHS for the purpose of hiring such personnel.
Additionally, the bill requires DHS to establish joint procedures to coordinate the efforts of various agencies within DHS with HSI's Cyber Crimes Center in child sexual exploitation investigations. The bill also authorizes the Cyber Crimes Center to establish joint procedures to coordinate with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) in child sexual exploitation investigations.
Finally, the bill directs DHS to establish a Victim Identification Training Program in the Cyber Crimes Center to help HSI personnel; federal state, local, tribal, and foreign law enforcement agency personnel; civil service organizations; and the NCMEC identify victims of sexual exploitation and abuse.
